title: When the Will Wakes
premise: True-crime podcaster Kestrel Fairweather receives a retainer from a nervous stranger who wants proof that a murder in the dying mill town of Hollow Creek hasn't happened yet — a murder foretold by a will that only activates upon a death that hasn't occurred. Digging into the town's coldest case, the twelve-year-old disappearance of Judge Aldous Wren, Kestrel discovers the judge never died: he's been hidden away, and his will is a ticking mechanism designed to expose the town's complicit families the moment he truly passes. As the statute of limitations closes and someone begins hunting both Kestrel and the hidden judge, Kestrel must choose between protecting the person they love — the judge's granddaughter, deputy Iris Wren — and dragging the whole town's guilt into daylight. In the end, Kestrel broadcasts the truth on air, forcing justice outside the courtroom, and loses the case file but keeps Iris.
about_author: Tamsin Hartwell is a former court stenographer from rural Vermont who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the secrets communities keep and the price of saying them out loud.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Kestrel Fairweather, POV. A cash-stuffed envelope arrives with no return address, paying Kestrel to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — dated twelve years forward. The emotional beat is uneasy curiosity; Kestrel, broke and bored after twelve years of safe episodes, pockets the money and starts asking questions they shouldn't.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We tour the archive: twelve years of Hollow Creek secrets filed and cross-referenced, including the closed case of Judge Aldous Wren's disappearance. A listener email flags an inconsistency in the coroner's report. The beat is the comfort of order beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Deputy Wren
chapters.summary: Iris Wren's POV. Iris, the missing judge's granddaughter and the town's deputy, notices Kestrel sniffing around the courthouse records. Old attraction and old wariness collide; she warns Kestrel off. Emotional beat: loyalty to a town that raised her versus a itch of doubt she's never voiced.

chapters.title: The Will That Waits
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel obtains a sealed copy of Wren's will through a records clerk: it disperses everything only 'upon confirmed death,' yet probate closed years ago on a presumption of death no body ever supported. Beat: the first real vertigo — the case may not be cold, it may be fake.

chapters.title: Client Unknown
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Tracing the retainer leads to a shuttered law office and a burned ledger; someone has been paying an annual stipend to keep Wren's death presumed. Kestrel realizes their client may be inside the conspiracy — or its conscience. Beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: What the Mill Remembered
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Iris interviews a retired mill foreman for an unrelated case and hears about trucks leaving the Wren estate the night of the disappearance. She says nothing to her chief. Beat: the first deliberate act of disloyalty to the department, and it feels like relief.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel maps who benefited from Wren's presumed death: four founding families, the bank, the sheriff. An anonymous warning nails a dead crow to the studio door. Beat: fear sharpening into obsession; staying invisible was never really an option.

chapters.title: The House on Corvid Lane
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Iris breaks into the boarded Wren house and finds dust disturbed — someone has been living there, or visiting, for years. Fresh flowers on the mantel. Beat: hope she doesn't dare name; her grandfather might be alive, which means everyone lied to her.

chapters.title: Episode Ninety-One
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel airs a carefully vague episode about probate irregularities; within hours, two sources recant and one goes missing. The client calls for the first time — a distorted voice saying only, 'Stop before the statute does.' Beat: the investigation now has a clock.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Legal research reveals the window to reopen the case closes in nineteen days. Kestrel and Iris, forced together by converging evidence, form an uneasy alliance and agree to share what each knows. Beat: trust kindling between two people trained to distrust.

chapters.title: The Fourth Family
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Iris confronts her godmother, matriarch of the Ashcombe family, who neither confirms nor denies but slips her a key and says, 'He asked us to let him go.' Beat: grief and fury braided together; the conspiracy had dissenters all along.

chapters.title: Buried Alive, By Choice
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the key to a decommissioned sanatorium, Kestrel finds evidence Judge Wren faked his death to trigger his own will — a dead-man's switch meant to detonate the town's secrets upon his real passing. Someone has been keeping him alive, and hidden, ever since. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Who Keeps Him
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Iris identifies the caretaker: her own father, the judge's son, who has spent twelve years imprisoned by filial duty, keeping the secret that would ruin him too. Father and daughter collide. Beat: love against duty made flesh in one family.

chapters.title: The Middleman Dies
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The records clerk who leaked the will is found drowned — ruled accidental. Kestrel realizes the client's payments weren't protection money; they were hush installments, and the account just ran dry. Beat: survivor's guilt and the understanding that Kestrel is next.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Becomes Four
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The statute deadline accelerates when the district attorney moves to permanently seal the Wren file. Kestrel and Iris race to locate the living judge before the legal door shuts forever. Beat: breathless momentum, the net closing from every side.

chapters.title: Corvid Lane, Again
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Returning to the Wren house, Iris finds her father gone and a trail leading to the sanatorium — along with the sheriff's cruiser parked in the trees. The hunters have become the hunted. Beat: terror fused with resolve; there is no neutral ground left.

chapters.title: The Room at the End
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Kestrel and Iris find Judge Wren alive, frail, lucid, and furious that his instrument of justice was neutered for twelve years. He refuses rescue unless the truth airs first. Outside, the sheriff arrives. Beat: the moral crux — a man demanding justice outside the law, at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Standoff in the Long Ward
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Iris draws her weapon on her own chief to buy Kestrel time to reach the transmitter. Her father steps between them. Shots are fired; the caretaker-son is wounded shielding Iris. Beat: the climax's first detonation — duty shattering publicly, irreversibly.

chapters.title: On Air
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. From the sanatorium's old radio room, Kestrel streams live: the judge speaks, naming the four families, the forged coroner's report, the twelve years of paid silence. The town listens. The sheriff backs down under the weight of witnesses. Beat: catharsis — truth as the only verdict available.

chapters.title: Confirmed Death
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Hours after testifying on air, Judge Wren dies peacefully, his will finally executing as designed: assets flow to victims' descendants, and the sealed evidence unlocks automatically. Beat: elegiac triumph; the machine he built works, just late.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Arrests ripple through Hollow Creek; Iris resigns rather than swear loyalty to a department she no longer trusts, then accepts a state investigator's badge. Her father faces charges and asks her not to visit. Beat: costly justice — every gain itemized against what it took.

chapters.title: The Next Envelope
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Months later, Kestrel and Iris, together, close the podcast's final episode on the Wren case. A new envelope arrives: another prepayment, another town, another secret. Kestrel looks at Iris, then at the envelope. Beat: quiet resolution with the door left open — some cases choose you.
